subtitle: Lesson 16 · Core ITIL 4 Practices: Incident, Problem & Change

code:
Purpose: maximize the number of successful
service and product changes, by ensuring risks
are properly assessed, authorizing changes to
proceed, and managing a change schedule.

Not: minimize changes.
Not: slow everything down.
caption: Renamed from "change management" in ITIL v3 to avoid confusion with organizational change management.

steps.label: Standard change
steps.sub: low-risk, well-understood, repeatable — pre-authorized, no sign-off needed each time

steps.label: Normal change
steps.sub: needs individual assessment and authorization through a defined process

steps.label: Emergency change
steps.sub: must happen ASAP, often to fix a major incident — expedited, but still authorized

code:
Standard change  -> pre-authorized model/template
Normal change    -> change authority reviews
                     risk, impact, rollback plan
Emergency change -> smaller group, fast review,
                     full documentation after
caption: Skipping authorization entirely isn't an emergency change — it's an unauthorized change.

subtitle: Three practices, one real loop that closes back on itself.
